current_example.title: Example: Evaluating a Triple Integral by Converting to Cylindrical Coordinates

q-161603.name: Question 1
q-161603.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=16$ between the surfaces $z=0$ and $z=\sqrt{25-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}.$ Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}z\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161603.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/5d8a94cd0df8095c78aec955c3d0f062e38410326399104644b24e981eb1db9a.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $4$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=0,$ and

- bounded above by $z=\sqrt{25-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}=\sqrt{25-{r}^{2}}.$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le 4,\,0\le \theta <2\pi ,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{25-{r}^{2}}\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}z\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}zr\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{25-{r}^{2}}}rz\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

q-161603.html:
Question 1
?

The region R is enclosed inside the cylinder x2+y2=16 between the surfaces z=0 and z=25−(x2+y2). Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates. ∭RzdV

a
∫02π∫04∫025−rrzdzdrdθ
b
∫02π∫04∫025−r2rzdzdrdθ
c
∫02π∫016∫025−r2zdzdrdθ
d
∫02π∫04∫025−r2zdzdrdθ
e
∫02π∫016∫025−rrzdzdrdθ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is a right vertical cylinder of radius 4 whose axis passes through the point (0,0) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=0, and

  • bounded above by z=25−(x2+y2)=25−r2.

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤4,0≤θ<2π,0≤z≤25−r2}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭RzdV=∭Δzrdzdrdθ=∫02π∫04∫025−r2rzdzdrdθ.

q-161520.name: Question 2
q-161520.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=25$  for $x\ge 0$ between the surfaces $z=0$ and $z=6+y.$
Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}xz\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161520.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/b194b4882dcada56a10ec69f9dae80b363ea05efaae27385ceacc9a15ba3b56f.png)

The region $R$ is one-half of a right vertical cylinder of radius $5$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=0,$ and

- bounded above by $z=6+y=6+r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le 5,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le z\le 6+r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}xz\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )z\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{6+r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{r}^{2}z\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

q-161520.html:
Question 2
?

The region R is enclosed inside the cylinder x2+y2=25 for x≥0 between the surfaces z=0 and z=6+y. Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates. ∭RxzdV

a
∫−π/2π/2∫05∫06+rsin⁡θrzcos⁡θdzdrdθ
b
∫0π/2∫05∫06+rcos⁡θrzsin⁡θdzdrdθ
c
∫0π/2∫05∫06+rsin⁡θr2zsin⁡θdzdrdθ
d
∫−π/2π/2∫05∫06+rcos⁡θr2zcos⁡θdzdrdθ
e
∫−π/2π/2∫05∫06+rsin⁡θr2zcos⁡θdzdrdθ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is one-half of a right vertical cylinder of radius 5 whose axis passes through the point (0,0) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=0, and

  • bounded above by z=6+y=6+rsin⁡θ.

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤5,−π2≤θ≤π2,0≤z≤6+rsin⁡θ}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭RxzdV=∭Δ(rcos⁡θ)zrdzdrdθ=∫−π/2π/2∫05∫06+rsin⁡θr2zcos⁡θdzdrdθ.

q-161609.name: Question 3
q-161609.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2$ for $x\ge 0$ and $y\ge 0,$ between the surfaces $z=1$ and $z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+4.$ Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}2xy\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161609.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/140ac7f7d6036657a4ba8a0c6944474c2aa0dfba7f7719228cdffb4d0cf9316f.png)

The region $R$ is one-quarter of a right vertical cylinder of radius $\sqrt{2}$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=1,$ and

- bounded above by $z={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+4={r}^{2}+4.$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le \sqrt{2},\,0\le \theta <\frac{\pi }{2},\,1\le z\le {r}^{2}+4\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}2xy\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}2(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\cdot r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{1}^{{r}^{2}+4}{r}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta \,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

q-161609.html:
Question 3
?

The region R is enclosed inside the cylinder x2+y2=2 for x≥0 and y≥0, between the surfaces z=1 and z=x2+y2+4. Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates. ∭R2xydV

a
∫0π/2∫02∫1r2+4r2sin⁡2θdzdrdθ
b
∫0π/2∫02∫1r2+4r3sin⁡2θdzdrdθ
c
∫0π/2∫02∫1r+4r3sin⁡2θdzdrdθ
d
∫0π∫02∫1r2+4r3sin⁡2θdzdrdθ
e
∫0π∫02∫1r+4r2sin⁡2θdzdrdθ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is one-quarter of a right vertical cylinder of radius 2 whose axis passes through the point (0,0) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=1, and

  • bounded above by z=x2+y2+4=r2+4.

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤2,0≤θ<π2,1≤z≤r2+4}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭R2xydV=∭Δ2(rcos⁡θ)(rsin⁡θ)⋅rdzdrdθ=∫0π/2∫02∫1r2+4r3sin⁡2θdzdrdθ.

q-161602.name: Question 4
q-161602.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=5$ between the surfaces $z=2$ and $z=4+y.$ Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}{z}^{2}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161602.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/286910d89e35603dc6558b80b11d06736d213fbad8c9c91825f42ff87b26e318.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $\sqrt{5}$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=2,$ and

- bounded above by $z=4+y=4+r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le \sqrt{5},\,0\le \theta <2\pi ,\,2\le z\le 4+r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{z}^{2}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{z}^{2}r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{5}}{\int }_{2}^{4+r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }r{z}^{2}\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

q-161602.html:
Question 4
?

The region R is enclosed inside the cylinder x2+y2=5 between the surfaces z=2 and z=4+y. Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates. ∭Rz2dV

a
∫02π∫05∫24+rsin⁡θrz2dzdrdθ
b
∫02π∫05∫24+rcos⁡θrz2dzdrdθ
c
∫02π∫05∫24r2z2dzdrdθ
d
∫02π∫05∫24rz2dzdrdθ
e
∫02π∫05∫24+rsin⁡θz2dzdrdθ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is a right vertical cylinder of radius 5 whose axis passes through the point (0,0) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=2, and

  • bounded above by z=4+y=4+rsin⁡θ.

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤5,0≤θ<2π,2≤z≤4+rsin⁡θ}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rz2dV=∭Δz2rdzdrdθ=∫02π∫05∫24+rsin⁡θrz2dzdrdθ.

q-161607.name: Question 5
q-161607.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2$ between the surfaces $z=0$ and $z=\sqrt{16-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}.$ Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+z}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161607.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/36839d1fbde65e86df7335d40374fe72a5ff43ed92b89405327406a62dc8763c.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $\sqrt{2}$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=0,$ and

- bounded above by $z=\sqrt{16-({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})}=\sqrt{16-{r}^{2}}.$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le \sqrt{2},\,0\le \theta <2\pi ,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{16-{r}^{2}}\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+z}}\cdot r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{16-{r}^{2}}}\frac{r}{\sqrt{1+z}}\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

The region R is enclosed inside the cylinder x2+y2=2 between the surfaces z=0 and z=16−(x2+y2). Express the following triple integral in cylindrical polar coordinates. ∭R11+zdV

a
∫02π∫02∫016−r2r1+zdzdrdθ
b
∫02π∫02∫04−rr1+zdzdrdθ
c
∫02π∫02∫04−r11+zdzdrdθ
d
∫02π∫02∫016−r211+zdzdrdθ
e
∫02π∫02∫016−r2r1+zdzdrdθ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is a right vertical cylinder of radius 2 whose axis passes through the point (0,0) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=0, and

  • bounded above by z=16−(x2+y2)=16−r2.

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤2,0≤θ<2π,0≤z≤16−r2}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭R1zdV=∭Δ11+z⋅rdzdrdθ=∫02π∫02∫016−r2r1+zdzdrdθ.
q-161607.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Triple Integral Defined Over a Cylindrical Solid

q-161521.name: Question 6
q-161521.problem:
If the solid region $R$ is given by 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2}\le 9,\,0\le z\le 2+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\},
$$

then ${∭}_{R}xy\,\text{d}V=$
q-161521.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/75bec31176c369e69d5b11af3eeab23f86a4f32251e37f56b225e9dd0bd4a3de.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $3$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,-3)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=0,$ and

- bounded above by $z=2+{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2+{r}^{2}.$

With that in mind, let's write the equation ${x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2}=9$ in polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+(y+3)^{2} & =9 \\ {(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{2}+{(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +3)}^{2} & =9 \\ {r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +6r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +9 & =9 \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+6r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ {r}^{2}+6r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ r(r+6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $r$ cannot be identical to zero on the entire circle, we must have $r=-6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le -6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\pi \le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le z\le 2+{r}^{2}\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}xy\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{-6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\int }_{0}^{2+{r}^{2}}{r}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

q-161521.html:
Question 6
?

If the solid region R is given by R={(x,y,z):x2+(y+3)2≤9,0≤z≤2+x2+y2}, then ∭RxydV=

a
∫π2π∫03∫02+rr2cos⁡θsin⁡θdzdrdθ
b
∫π2π∫03∫02+rr3cos⁡θsin⁡θdzdrdθ
c
∫π2π∫06cos⁡θ∫02+r2r3cos⁡θsin⁡θdzdrdθ
d
∫π2π∫0−6sin⁡θ∫02+r2r3cos⁡θsin⁡θdzdrdθ
e
∫π2π∫0−6sin⁡θ∫02+r2r2cos⁡θsin⁡θdzdrdθ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is a right vertical cylinder of radius 3 whose axis passes through the point (0,−3) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=0, and

  • bounded above by z=2+x2+y2=2+r2.

With that in mind, let's write the equation x2+(y+3)2=9 in polar coordinates:

x2+(y+3)2=9(rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ+3)2=9r2cos2⁡θ+r2sin2⁡θ+6rsin⁡θ+9=9r2(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)+6rsin⁡θ=0r2+6rsin⁡θ=0r(r+6sin⁡θ)=0

Since r cannot be identical to zero on the entire circle, we must have r=−6sin⁡θ.

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤−6sin⁡θ,π≤θ≤2π,0≤z≤2+r2}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭RxydV=∭Δ(rcos⁡θ)(rsin⁡θ)rdzdrdθ=∫π2π∫0−6sin⁡θ∫02+r2r3cos⁡θsin⁡θdzdrdθ.

q-161628.name: Question 7
q-161628.problem:
If the solid region $R$ is given by 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x-2)^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 4,\,y-4\le z\le 3\},
$$

then ${∭}_{R}z\,\text{d}V=$
q-161628.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/a6b6faca2cd9cb66d463178a24efeb6f47d1dfa0bffe17c657e0d0be2dd11426.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $2$ whose axis passes through the point $(2,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=y-4=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -4,$ and

- bounded above by $z=3.$

With that in mind, let's write the equation $(x-2)^{2}+{y}^{2}=4$ in polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2}+{y}^{2} & =4 \\ {(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -2)}^{2}+{(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2} & =4 \\ {r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -4r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +4+{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =4 \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )-4r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ {r}^{2}-4r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ r(r-4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $r$ cannot be identical to zero on the entire circle, we must have $r=4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le 4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -4\le z\le 3\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}z\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}zr\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{4\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\int }_{r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -4}^{3}rz\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

q-161628.html:
Question 7
?

If the solid region R is given by R={(x,y,z):(x−2)2+y2≤4,y−4≤z≤3}, then ∭RzdV=

a
∫−π/2π/2∫04sin⁡θ∫rsin⁡θ−43r2zdzdrdθ
b
∫−π/2π/2∫04sin⁡θ∫rsin⁡θ−43rzdzdrdθ
c
∫−π/2π/2∫04cos⁡θ∫rcos⁡θ−43rzdzdrdθ
d
∫−π/2π/2∫04cos⁡θ∫rsin⁡θ−43zdzdrdθ
e
∫−π/2π/2∫04cos⁡θ∫rsin⁡θ−43rzdzdrdθ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is a right vertical cylinder of radius 2 whose axis passes through the point (2,0) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=y−4=rsin⁡θ−4, and

  • bounded above by z=3.

With that in mind, let's write the equation (x−2)2+y2=4 in polar coordinates: (x−2)2+y2=4(rcos⁡θ−2)2+(rsin⁡θ)2=4r2cos2⁡θ−4rcos⁡θ+4+r2sin2⁡θ=4r2(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)−4rcos⁡θ=0r2−4rcos⁡θ=0r(r−4cos⁡θ)=0

Since r cannot be identical to zero on the entire circle, we must have r=4cos⁡θ.

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤4cos⁡θ,−π2≤θ≤π2,rsin⁡θ−4≤z≤3}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭RzdV=∭Δzrdzdrdθ=∫−π/2π/2∫04cos⁡θ∫rsin⁡θ−43rzdzdrdθ.
q-161628.knowledge_point: Rewriting a Triple Integral Defined Over a Shifted Cylindrical Solid

q-161630.name: Question 8
q-161630.problem:
If the solid region $R$ is given by 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(x+3)^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 9,\,-8\le z\le x+2\},
$$

then ${∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}V=$
q-161630.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/3c03dde21942c60de527ace896bb51ad8070781126d72f5be5e2f6069700736d.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $3$ whose axis passes through the point $(-3,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=-8,$ and

- bounded above by $z=x+2=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +2.$

With that in mind, let's write the equation $(x+3)^{2}+{y}^{2}=9$ in polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+3)^{2}+{y}^{2} & =9 \\ {(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +3)}^{2}+{(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2} & =9 \\ {r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +6r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +9+{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  & =9 \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+6r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ {r}^{2}+6r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ r(r+6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $r$ cannot be identical to zero on the entire circle, we must have $r=-6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le -6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,-8\le z\le r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +2\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{1}{\sqrt{(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}+1}}\cdot r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{r}{\sqrt{{r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+1}}\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{-6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\int }_{-8}^{r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +2}\frac{r}{\sqrt{{r}^{2}+1}}\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

q-161630.html:
Question 8
?

If the solid region R is given by R={(x,y,z):(x+3)2+y2≤9,−8≤z≤x+2}, then ∭R1x2+y2+1dV=

a
∫π/23π/2∫0−6cos⁡θ∫−8rcos⁡θ+21r2+1dzdrdθ
b
∫π/23π/2∫0−6sin⁡θ∫−8rcos⁡θ+2rr2+1dzdrdθ
c
∫π/23π/2∫0−6sin⁡θ∫−8rsin⁡θ+21r2+1dzdrdθ
d
∫π/23π/2∫0−6cos⁡θ∫−8rcos⁡θ+2rr2+1dzdrdθ
e
∫π/23π/2∫0−6cos⁡θ∫−8rsin⁡θ+2rr2+1dzdrdθ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is a right vertical cylinder of radius 3 whose axis passes through the point (−3,0) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=−8, and

  • bounded above by z=x+2=rcos⁡θ+2.

With that in mind, let's write the equation (x+3)2+y2=9 in polar coordinates: (x+3)2+y2=9(rcos⁡θ+3)2+(rsin⁡θ)2=9r2cos2⁡θ+6rcos⁡θ+9+r2sin2⁡θ=9r2(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)+6rcos⁡θ=0r2+6rcos⁡θ=0r(r+6cos⁡θ)=0

Since r cannot be identical to zero on the entire circle, we must have r=−6cos⁡θ.

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤−6cos⁡θ,π2≤θ≤3π2,−8≤z≤rcos⁡θ+2}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭R1x2+y2+1dV=∭Δ1(rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ)2+1⋅rdzdrdθ=∭Δrr2(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)+1dzdrdθ=∫π/23π/2∫0−6cos⁡θ∫−8rcos⁡θ+2rr2+1dzdrdθ.

q-161637.name: Question 9
q-161637.problem:
If the solid region $R$ is given by 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}+(y-4)^{2}\le 16,\,x\ge 0,\,-5\le z\le x\},
$$

then ${∭}_{R}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}V=$
q-161637.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/b66b8db18b2f5773addc2d00c02f2f15f4a7ead53323418e63bd50457f74466b.png)

The region $R$ is one-half of a right vertical cylinder of radius $4$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,4)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=-5,$ and

- bounded above by $z=x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

With that in mind, let's now write the ${x}^{2}+(y-4)^{2}=16$ in polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+(y-4)^{2} & =16 \\ (r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -4)^{2} & =16 \\ {r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta -8r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +16 & =16 \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )-8r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ {r}^{2}-8r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ r(r-8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $r$ cannot be identical to zero on the entire semicircle, we must have $r=8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le 8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2},\,-5\le z\le r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\sqrt{(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}+1}\cdot r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}\sqrt{{r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+1}\cdot r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{8\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\int }_{-5}^{r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }r\sqrt{{r}^{2}+1}\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

q-161637.html:
Question 9
?

If the solid region R is given by R={(x,y,z):x2+(y−4)2≤16,x≥0,−5≤z≤x}, then ∭Rx2+y2+1dV=

a
∫0π/2∫08sin⁡θ∫−5rsin⁡θrr2+1dzdrdθ
b
∫0π/2∫08sin⁡θ∫−5rcos⁡θr2+1dzdrdθ
c
∫0π∫08sin⁡θ∫−5rsin⁡θr2+1dzdrdθ
d
∫0π/2∫08sin⁡θ∫−5rcos⁡θrr2+1dzdrdθ
e
∫0π∫08sin⁡θ∫−5rcos⁡θrr2+1dzdrdθ
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is one-half of a right vertical cylinder of radius 4 whose axis passes through the point (0,4) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=−5, and

  • bounded above by z=x=rcos⁡θ.

With that in mind, let's now write the x2+(y−4)2=16 in polar coordinates: x2+(y−4)2=16(rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ−4)2=16r2cos2⁡θ+r2sin2⁡θ−8rsin⁡θ+16=16r2(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)−8rsin⁡θ=0r2−8rsin⁡θ=0r(r−8sin⁡θ)=0

Since r cannot be identical to zero on the entire semicircle, we must have r=8sin⁡θ.

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤8sin⁡θ,0≤θ≤π2,−5≤z≤rcos⁡θ}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain
∭Rx2+y2+1dV=∭Δ(rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ)2+1⋅rdzdrdθ=∭Δr2(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)+1⋅rdzdrdθ=∫0π/2∫08sin⁡θ∫−5rcos⁡θrr2+1dzdrdθ.

q-161631.name: Question 10
q-161631.problem:
If the solid region $R$ is given by 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,{x}^{2}+(y+2)^{2}\le 4,\,-y-3\le z\le 3\},
$$

then ${∭}_{R}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1\,\text{d}V=$
q-161631.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/b1886315cede967bc6fd606cdf7bf9d6ae4f82264ccce22211562aa590a8fe4a.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $2$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,-2)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=-y-3=-r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -3,$ and

- bounded above by $z=3.$

With that in mind, let's write the equation ${x}^{2}+(y+2)^{2}=4$ in polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+(y+2)^{2} & =4 \\ {(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{2}+{(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2)}^{2} & =4 \\ {r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +4r{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +4 & =4 \\ {r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+4r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ {r}^{2}+4r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & =0 \\ r(r+4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $r$ cannot be identical to zero on the entire circle, we must have $r=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le -4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\pi \le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,-r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -3\le z\le 3\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+1\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}({(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2}+1)\cdot r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={∭}_{Δ}({r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+1)\cdot r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{-4\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\int }_{-r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -3}^{3}r({r}^{2}+1)\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

q-161631.html:
Question 10
?

If the solid region R is given by R={(x,y,z):x2+(y+2)2≤4,−y−3≤z≤3}, then ∭Rx2+y2+1dV=

a
∫π2π∫0−4sin⁡θ∫−rcos⁡θ−33r2+1dzdrdθ
b
∫π2π∫0−4sin⁡θ∫−rsin⁡θ−33r(r2+1)dzdrdθ
c
∫02π∫0−4sin⁡θ∫−rcos⁡θ−33r(r2+1)dzdrdθ
d
∫02π∫0−4sin⁡θ∫−rsin⁡θ−33r(r2+1)dzdrdθ
e
∫π2π∫0−4sin⁡θ∫−rsin⁡θ−33r2+1dzdrdθ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is a right vertical cylinder of radius 2 whose axis passes through the point (0,−2) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=−y−3=−rsin⁡θ−3, and

  • bounded above by z=3.

With that in mind, let's write the equation x2+(y+2)2=4 in polar coordinates: x2+(y+2)2=4(rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ+2)2=4r2cos2⁡θ+r2sin2⁡θ+4rsin2⁡θ+4=4r2(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)+4rsin⁡θ=0r2+4rsin⁡θ=0r(r+4sin⁡θ)=0

Since r cannot be identical to zero on the entire circle, we must have r=−4sin⁡θ.

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤−4sin⁡θ,π≤θ≤2π,−rsin⁡θ−3≤z≤3}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rx2+y2+1dV=∭Δ((rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ)2+1)⋅rdzdrdθ=∭Δ(r2(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)+1)⋅rdzdrdθ=∫π2π∫0−4sin⁡θ∫−rsin⁡θ−33r(r2+1)dzdrdθ.

q-161617.name: Question 11
q-161617.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{z}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=9$ and between the surfaces $z=0$ and $z=\sqrt{9-({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})}.$
q-161617.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/9c4ea0ba92e19a201e3944defa6deb0bc1ee76971adaa809521722b6ac31241f.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $3$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=0,$ and

- bounded above by $z=\sqrt{9-({x}^{2}-{y}^{2})}=\sqrt{9-{r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}=\sqrt{9-{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )}.$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le 3,\,0\le \theta <2\pi ,\,0\le z\le \sqrt{9-{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )}\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{z}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{z}{\sqrt{{r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{r}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }}\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{9-{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )}}z\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}{[\frac{1}{2}{z}^{2}]}_{z=0}^{z=\sqrt{9-{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )}}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{2}{(\sqrt{9-{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )})}^{2}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{2}(9-{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ))\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{[\frac{9}{2}r-\frac{1}{6}{r}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )]}_{r=0}^{r=3}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{9}{2}(3)-\frac{1}{6}(3)^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{27}{2}-\frac{9}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={[\frac{27}{2}\theta -\frac{9}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )]}_{\theta =0}^{\theta =2\pi } \\  & =\frac{27}{2}(2\pi -0)-\frac{9}{4}(0-0) \\  & =27\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Evaluate the triple integral ∭Rzx2+y2dV over the region R enclosed inside the cylinder x2+y2=9 and between the surfaces z=0 and z=9−(x2−y2).

a
 27π
b
 19π3
c
 9π
d
 9π2
e
 54π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is a right vertical cylinder of radius 3 whose axis passes through the point (0,0) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=0, and

  • bounded above by z=9−(x2−y2)=9−r2(cos2⁡θ−sin2⁡θ)=9−r2cos⁡(2θ).

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤3,0≤θ<2π,0≤z≤9−r2cos⁡(2θ)}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rzx2+y2dV=∭Δzr2cos2⁡θ+r2sin⁡θrdzdrdθ=∫02π∫03∫09−r2cos⁡(2θ)zdzdrdθ=∫02π∫03[12z2]z=0z=9−r2cos⁡(2θ)drdθ=∫02π∫0312(9−r2cos⁡(2θ))2drdθ=∫02π∫0312(9−r2cos⁡(2θ))drdθ=∫02π[92r−16r3cos⁡(2θ)]r=0r=3dθ=∫02π92(3)−16(3)3cos⁡(2θ)dθ=∫02π272−92cos⁡(2θ)dθ=[272θ−94sin⁡(2θ)]θ=0θ=2π=272(2π−0)−94(0−0)=27π.

q-161615.name: Question 12
q-161615.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=3$ for $x\ge 0$ and between the surfaces $z=y$ and $z=y+4.$
q-161615.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/e289cfbd210112a619018a7b905f7f2b1a9859ecb84b2517dd745705624d79d7.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $\sqrt{3}$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ and

- bounded above by $z=y+4=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +4.$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le \sqrt{3},\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta <\frac{\pi }{2},\,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \le z\le r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +4\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \sqrt{(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}}\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}{\int }_{r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }^{r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +4}{r}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}{r}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta [z]_{z=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }^{z=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +4}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}{r}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta (r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +4-r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}4{r}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}[{r}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ]_{r=0}^{r=\sqrt{3}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}(\sqrt{3})^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}9\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =[9\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]_{\theta =-\pi /2}^{\theta =\pi /2} \\  & =9(1-(-1)) \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161615.html:
Question 12
?

Evaluate the triple integral ∭Rxx2+y2dV over the region R enclosed inside the cylinder x2+y2=3 for x≥0 and between the surfaces z=y and z=y+4.

a
 12π
b
 15π2
c
 9π2
d
 18
e
 9π
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is a right vertical cylinder of radius 3 whose axis passes through the point (0,0) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=y=rsin⁡θ, and

  • bounded above by z=y+4=rsin⁡θ+4.

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤3,−π2≤θ<π2,rsin⁡θ≤z≤rsin⁡θ+4}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rxx2+y2dV=∭Δrcos⁡θ(rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ)2rdzdrdθ=∫−π/2π/2∫03∫rsin⁡θrsin⁡θ+4r3cos⁡θdzdrdθ=∫−π/2π/2∫03r3cos⁡θ[z]z=rsin⁡θz=rsin⁡θ+4drdθ=∫−π/2π/2∫03r3cos⁡θ(rsin⁡θ+4−rsin⁡θ)drdθ=∫−π/2π/2∫034r3cos⁡θdrdθ=∫−π/2π/2[r4cos⁡θ]r=0r=3dθ=∫−π/2π/2(3)4cos⁡θdθ=∫−π/2π/29cos⁡θdθ=[9sin⁡θ]θ=−π/2θ=π/2=9(1−(−1))=18.

q-161608.name: Question 13
q-161608.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1$ and between the surfaces $z=0$ and $z=4-x.$
q-161608.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/62abd56d2d374afb7c608aa64f701cfe94f096b823f964697a929c7c24f3a073.png)

The region $R$ is a right vertical cylinder of radius $1$ whose axis passes through the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=0,$ and

- bounded above by $z=4-x=4-r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le 1,\,0\le \theta <2\pi ,\,0\le z\le 4-r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}({(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )}^{2}+{(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2})\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{4-r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{r}^{3}\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}{r}^{3}[z]_{z=0}^{z=4-r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}{r}^{3}(4-r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}4{r}^{3}-{r}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{[{r}^{4}-\frac{1}{5}{r}^{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ]}_{r=0}^{r=1}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }1-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =[\theta -\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]_{\theta =0}^{\theta =2\pi } \\  & =(2\pi -0)-\frac{1}{5}(0-0) \\  & =2\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is a right vertical cylinder of radius 1 whose axis passes through the point (0,0) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=0, and

  • bounded above by z=4−x=4−rcos⁡θ.

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤1,0≤θ<2π,0≤z≤4−rcos⁡θ}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rx2+y2dV=∭Δ((rcos⁡θ)2+(rsin⁡θ)2)rdzdrdθ=∫02π∫01∫04−rcos⁡θr3dzdrdθ=∫02π∫01r3[z]z=0z=4−rcos⁡θdrdθ=∫02π∫01r3(4−rcos⁡θ)drdθ=∫02π∫014r3−r4cos⁡θdrdθ=∫02π[r4−15r5cos⁡θ]r=0r=1dθ=∫02π1−15cos⁡θdθ=[θ−15sin⁡θ]θ=0θ=2π=(2π−0)−15(0−0)=2π.

q-40785.name: Question 14
q-40785.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}2z\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the cylinder ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=9$  for $y\ge 0$ and between the surfaces $z=-x$ and $z=2+x.$
q-40785.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14235769/assets/063fafc4f8c50dba56bcfb50b8366a2ffb8c713f5668ce22d10c0370376bbaba.png)

The region $R$ is one-half of a right vertical cylinder of radius $3$ whose axis passes through the point $(1,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=-x=-r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ and

- bounded above by $z=2+x=2+r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta ,z)\,:\,0\le r\le 3,\,0\le \theta \le \pi ,\,-r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \le z\le 2+r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}2z\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}2z\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{-r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }^{2+r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }2rz\,dz\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}r[{z}^{2}]_{z=-r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }^{z=2+r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}r((2+r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}-(-r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2})\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}4r+4{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{[2{r}^{2}+\frac{4}{3}{r}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ]}_{r=0}^{r=3}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }2(3)^{2}+\frac{4}{3}(3)^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }18+36\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =[18\theta +36\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ]_{\theta =0}^{\theta =\pi } \\  & =18(\pi -0)+36(0-0) \\  & =18\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

q-40785.html:
Question 14
?

Evaluate the triple integral ∭R2zdV over the region R enclosed inside the cylinder x2+y2=9 for y≥0 and between the surfaces z=−x and z=2+x.

a
18π
b
35π2
c
10π
d
27π2
e
15π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(rcos⁡θ,rsin⁡θ,z)rdzdrdθ.

If (r,θ,z) are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the formulas

x=rcos⁡θ,y=rsin⁡θ,z=z.

First, let's sketch the projection of R onto the xy-plane:

The region R is one-half of a right vertical cylinder of radius 3 whose axis passes through the point (1,0) in the xy-plane, and is

  • bounded below by z=−x=−rcos⁡θ, and

  • bounded above by z=2+x=2+rcos⁡θ.

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(r,θ,z):0≤r≤3,0≤θ≤π,−rcos⁡θ≤z≤2+rcos⁡θ}.

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭R2zdV=∭Δ2zrdzdrdθ=∫0π∫03∫−rcos⁡θ2+rcos⁡θ2rzdzdrdθ=∫0π∫03r[z2]z=−rcos⁡θz=2+rcos⁡θdrdθ=∫0π∫03r((2+rcos⁡θ)2−(−rcos⁡θ)2)drdθ=∫0π∫034r+4r2cos⁡θdrdθ=∫0π[2r2+43r3cos⁡θ]r=0r=3dθ=∫0π2(3)2+43(3)3cos⁡θdθ=∫0π18+36cos⁡θdθ=[18θ+36sin⁡θ]θ=0θ=π=18(π−0)+36(0−0)=18π.
